clue.text: Composer's last in alphabetical order in directory

indicators.note: the second in places the final alphabet letter inside the word for a directory

parts.note: a directory is a list of names
Z is the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A composer's name comes last when a directory is sorted alphabetically.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has' and joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Delivery-man makes the most of two parties

indicators.note: taking the most of each party name means each loses its final letter here

parts.note: Liberal and Tory are two British political parties
Liberal and Tory are two British political parties

explanation.surface: A delivery driver gets the best out of a couple of celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes the most of' drops the last letter of each party: LIBERA from LIBERAL and TOR from TORY. 'Delivery-man' looks like a courier but means one who delivers people from captivity.
explanation.definitionFit: One who delivers or sets free people from oppression is their freer, a liberating figure.

clue.text: First light from star on high

parts.note: the sun is our nearest star
up means aloft, on high

explanation.surface: Dawn's first glow comes from a star high in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunrise, when daylight first appears, is the dawn moment.

clue.text: Riding speed that's far from ideal

parts.note: a riding was one of the three divisions of Yorkshire, the word coming from Old Norse for a third part
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A horse's riding pace that falls well short of perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire was historically split into three Ridings, North, East and West; the name means a third.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of poor, inferior quality is far from ideal.

clue.text: Source of serenity of daring characters, perhaps

definitions.text: Source of serenity of daring characters, perhaps

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter
the characters of the following words are taken as letters that may be rearranged

explanation.surface: What keeps bold people calm under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of' gives S from 'serenity'; 'characters, perhaps' shuffles OF DARING into ANGFROID. The whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Composure and coolness under pressure is the calm quality daring people draw upon.

clue.text: Suave type, like Jacob

explanation.surface: A charming smoothie compared with the biblical Jacob.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Jacob says 'my brother Esau is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man'.
explanation.definitionFit: A suave type is a smooth-talking charmer; Jacob, unlike hairy Esau, had smooth skin.

clue.text: As Leo's share is, certainly

explanation.surface: Describing a lion's portion with emphatic agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo is the lion, and the lion's share is much more than half; 'not half!' is British slang for 'definitely'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion's share exceeds a mere fifty per cent; the slang exclamation means emphatically yes.

clue.text: Half of score the minimum for this game?

definitions.text: Half of score the minimum for this game?

parts.words: Half of score the minimum for this game?
parts.note: a score is twenty and half is ten, which is two lots of five, the plural number name doubling as a handball court game

explanation.surface: Wondering whether ten points is the least you need to win a game.
explanation.walkthrough: FIVES is a British handball game played against walls; ten is made of two fives.
explanation.definitionFit: A court game where players strike a ball with gloved hands, played at English schools.

clue.text: Correct about the width of the hips

definitions.text: about the width of the hips

explanation.surface: Remarking accurately on how broad someone's hips are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the beam' means on course, correct; 'broad in the beam' describes wide hips.
explanation.definitionFit: Following a radio guidance signal means being on course, accurate; a beam is also a ship's width, used jokingly of hips.

clue.text: Skilful new driver in Dutch town

indicators.note: the learner is placed in the word for skilful

parts.note: deft means skilful, nimble
L stands for learner, the plate a new driver displays in Britain

explanation.surface: A capable learner driver is navigating a Netherlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers display an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is a city in the Netherlands famous for blue-and-white pottery.

clue.text: Ring one bird or animal in Australia

parts.note: a band is a ring, as a wedding band
I is the Roman numeral for one
a coot is a black water bird

explanation.surface: Ringing a bird or other creature in Australia for tracking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a verb for tagging birds; it is the noun BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A small marsupial native to Australia with a long pointed snout.

clue.text: Retrospective legislative section is essential

indicators.note: looking back, so the letters are read from right to left
a section of the word legislative is taken, part of its run of letters

explanation.surface: A section of law that applies backdated is crucially important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'section' takes LATIV from the middle of 'legislative'; 'Retrospective' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absolutely necessary or indispensable is vital.

clue.text: Attack around stern of ship in fleet

indicators.note: the word for attack goes around the end letter of ship

parts.note: a raid is an attack

indicators.note: the stern is the rear of a ship, so the final letter

explanation.surface: An assault on the back of a ship within a naval fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' is a naval squadron on the surface but the adjective meaning swift.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means swift or quick-moving.

clue.text: Changing instanter?

indicators.note: changing the letters of instanter rearranges them into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether something immediate is also fleeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instanter' is an old legal word for 'immediately'; the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something momentary and passing, here one minute and gone the next, is always changing.

clue.text: Scrap any thin fabric

parts.note: a scrap is a quarrel, a tiff
taken as written

explanation.surface: Discard any flimsy cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' reads as a verb meaning throw away, but it is a noun meaning a squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheer, gauze-like muslin or silk material.

clue.text: Mental abilities found in university

explanation.surface: Brainpower to be discovered at a college.
explanation.definitionFit: The mind's powers such as reason; also departments or schools of a university, such as law or arts.

clue.text: One of those in first gear

definitions.text: One of those in first gear

parts.words: One of those in first gear
parts.note: gear means clothing, and the first clothing was what Adam and Eve wore in Eden

explanation.surface: A car pulling away in its lowest gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first gear' looks motoring but means the very first garments ever worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam and Eve covered themselves with the leaves of a tree, the first clothes in Genesis.

clue.text: Being excessive in investigation

explanation.surface: Overdoing it in an inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: Exceeding a limit is overstepping it; a thorough examination or inspection is also called this.

clue.text: Burns supper suitable for this aggressive type?

definitions.text: Burns supper suitable for this aggressive type?

parts.words: Burns supper suitable for this aggressive type?
parts.note: burns read as flames rather than the poet, a meal of flames suits a performer who swallows them, also a hot-tempered person

explanation.surface: A Scottish poet's anniversary dinner seems just right for a combative guest.
explanation.walkthrough: A Burns supper is a Scottish dinner held on 25 January honouring the poet Robert Burns.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrelsome, belligerent person; also a performer who swallows flames.

clue.text: Another game controlled by tennis players

explanation.surface: A different match in the hands of tennis players.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast court game related to squash; tennis players also hold and swing bats with strings.

clue.text: Raced round edge and escaped

indicators.note: the word for raced goes round the word for edge

parts.note: sped means raced
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted round the boundary and got away.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipped away means got free or escaped unnoticed.

clue.text: Careless reader gets the bird

explanation.surface: A sloppy reader is given the bird, booed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' suggests being jeered, but the bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: One who reads quickly and superficially; also a seabird that flies low catching fish from the surface.

clue.text: Poet like Crabbe, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals the word is said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: Crabbe sounds like crab, and a crab is shelly, having a hard shell

explanation.surface: Comparing one poet to another poet, George Crabbe.
explanation.walkthrough: George Crabbe was himself an English poet, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe Shelley was an English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Bloomer in pantomime

explanation.surface: A blunder made during a Christmas stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flower; pantomime is a British Christmas theatre tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden flower, aquilegia; also Harlequin's sweetheart in traditional pantomime.

clue.text: Forcibly put end to infatuation

explanation.surface: Violently ending a passion.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppress a rebellion by force; also a brief intense infatuation.

clue.text: Intelligent lot for board of Roman company

explanation.surface: Bright people standing in for the directors of an Italian firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' means table: mensa is Latin for table.
explanation.definitionFit: The society for people with high IQs; also the Latin word for table, where Romans dined in company.

clue.text: Critic's craft seen in ego-trip

indicators.note: the ship letters are seen in the jumbled ego
a trip is a stumble, so the letters of ego are tumbled

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: A reviewer's skill is on display in a vanity project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like skill but means a vessel, and 'ego-trip' reads as vanity though it splits into fodder and anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Gosse was a Victorian English literary critic and author.

clue.text: Wife's loud complaint cut short

indicators.note: the noisy word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a squawk is a loud, harsh complaint

explanation.surface: A wife's noisy protest is interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: An old, now offensive term for a Native American wife or woman.

clue.text: Harmony in US or USSR. say

explanation.surface: Agreement within superpowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreement or concord; both the United States and the Soviet Union were federations, the U in each abbreviation.

clue.text: Staff underground room, in the event of high-level negotiations

parts.note: a pole is a staff
a vault is an underground chamber

explanation.surface: Office staff in a basement room during summit talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiations' looks diplomatic but means getting over a high bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An athletics field event in which jumpers clear a high bar using a long flexible rod.

clue.text: Even a single farmer may practice it

definitions.text: Even a single farmer may practice it

parts.words: Even a single farmer may practice it
parts.note: single read as unmarried, which seems at odds with a word containing a married man, yet it means farming

explanation.surface: Any farmer, even an unmarried one, can engage in this.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the word starts with HUSBAND, yet it means farming, open to bachelors too.
explanation.definitionFit: The care of crops and livestock; agriculture and careful management.

clue.text: Quarrelsome crewman?

parts.note: row read as quarrel, rhyming with cow, gives one who argues, but the word is an oarsman

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered member of a ship's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: Row rhymes with 'cow' when it means a quarrel, and with 'go' when it means using oars.
explanation.definitionFit: An oarsman in a boat's crew; jokingly, one who has quarrels.
